parole.significato: Among the ancient Maya people, a member of the leading class of nobles in a particular polity.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Yucatec Maya ajaw, ultimately from Proto-Mayan *ajahw.

parole.significato: A kind of sprite in the folklore of certain Maya peoples.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Yucatec Maya alux or via Spanish alux.

parole.significato: A stylized, pre-Columbian Mesoamerican stone sculpture depicting a reclining male figure with the head raised and turne…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Yucatec Maya chak moʼol (“jaguar”, literally “red paw”). The name was first given by Augustus Le Plongeon to a statue of this type discovered at Chichén Itzá in 1875.

parole.significato: A kind of ritual buffoon or clown in Yucatec Maya culture.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Yucatec Maya chiʼik (“coati; buffoon”).

parole.significato: a ceremonial ball game once played by the Aztecs and Maya; evolved into the ulama game.
A spicy yellow chili pepper used in Yucatecan cuisine.
parole.testo: From Yucatec Maya xkat-ik; -ik means “chili pepper”.
